method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across what remains of a life, remembered companionship, learning and the written record, grief and lament, care for survivors, character as inheritance, parents and kin, women’s faith and service, children and youth, sustained service, persecution and martyrdom, journeys toward presence, and prayer and visitation. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Khusraw is a person of pleasant countenance and good nature, faithful, truthful, and a kind friend
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing Khusraw as pleasant, faithful, truthful and a kind friend; praise of a living friend beside memorials of the dead.

selected.text: We were with her at the time of her ascension, and We made mention of her before and after her passing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that He was with a woman at the time of her ascension and mentioned her before and after her passing; nearness at death in a single sentence.

selected.text: Blessed are ye, for ye were endowed with faith in days when trembling seized the limbs of all religions.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: She was the very essence of loyalty. She assisted the believers very much and served them without ostentation.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a woman who was the essence of loyalty and served the believers without ostentation; service without display.

selected.text: Go every year to visit the grave of Mr Chase on my behalf, for he was a sanctified soul; his station will be known later.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the friends to visit Mr. Chase’s grave every year on His behalf; a practical obligation of remembrance.

selected.text: He is the Eternal! … Verily, the exalted leaf hath heard the call of the divine Lote-Tree and hath taken her flight unto it
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words on the gravestone of the wife of the Báb, that the exalted leaf has heard the call and taken flight; a memorial text in its own setting.

selected.text: The handmaiden of God, Lua, has hastened from this world to another world … you should speak well of her in every gathering
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Lua’s passing, asking that she be spoken well of in every gathering; a practical instruction for remembrance.

selected.text: Those days were marvelously pleasant! Turks have a saying, "The memory and reminiscence of those days are worth the world!"
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling pleasant days with the Turkish saying that their memory is worth the world; opens the companionship section with warmth.

selected.text: Lua, Juliet, May, Ella--how attached to each other they are! … Poor Lua! She is no more. She is very happy in the Kingdom of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Lua, Juliet, May and Ella, so attached to each other, and that Lua is now happy in the Kingdom; women’s companionship remembered.

selected.text: That branch offered up his soul in the flower of his youth and with the utmost joy and gladness he hastened to the realm beyond.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on a branch who offered up his soul in the flower of his youth with utmost joy; revealed testimony to a young life.

selected.text: and attracts the attention of souls. As for the passing of Engineer Volkov, the faithful architect of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar - truly this faithful architect strove in service
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the passing of Engineer Volkov, the faithful architect of the Mashriqu’l-Adhkár who strove in service; a distinctive practical legacy.

selected.text: You will observe the results of this ascension later in his lineage, as divine favors will encompass them and eternal gifts will be attained.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the results of a believer’s ascension will be seen later in his lineage; legacy in descendants.

selected.text: After the ascension of the Blessed Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones - 'Abdu'l-Baha was never so affected by any calamity.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that since the ascension of the Blessed Beauty He had never been so affected by any calamity; the measure of a single loss.

selected.text: Verily, thy father hath ascended unto God, and he is in a praiseworthy station. We have, of a truth, forgiven him as a token of Our grace unto him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assuring a child that his father is in a praiseworthy station and has been forgiven as a token of grace; revealed forgiveness for the departed.

selected.text: Verily Your servant Nazim was one who suppressed anger and forgave sins and harm, showing kindness to enemies even if they were the most bitter foes
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Nazim, who suppressed anger and showed kindness even to bitter foes; a brief, pointed portrait of character.

selected.text: Praise be to God that thou hast shown forth a white hand and hast written the history of the martyrs in most eloquent terms and most wondrous allusions
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising a believer who wrote the history of the martyrs in eloquent terms; carries the arc’s writing of history.

selected.text: Although that cherished maidservant of God hastened from this mortal world to the eternal realm, yet praise be to God that she left you as her memorial
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a maidservant of God has left her child as her memorial; the survivor as the living remembrance.

selected.text: The ascension of your parents greatly saddened my heart, for Jinab-i-Samandar was my helper and supporter, but as a swift-winged bird he ascended quickly.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saddened by the passing of Samandar, His helper, who ascended quickly like a swift-winged bird; personal grief briefly stated.

selected.text: O how I bewail this grief to You! Alas, then alas for his ascension to the Supreme Concourse. Never has time seen among the souls of the Shi'ih one like him.
selected.reason: The Báb bewailing a believer’s ascension and saying time has never seen one like him; the Báb’s voice of grief.

selected.text: His Holiness 'Abdu'llah, from the Most Glorious Kingdom, offers you a thousand praises, for praise be to God, after his passing you have acquitted yourself well
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the departed ‘Abdu’lláh offers a thousand praises because his survivor has acquitted himself well; the departed’s regard for conduct after a death.

selected.text: O fragrances of God! Pass by, perfumed with ambergris, over the earth wherein lies one who turned to God and returned to God, tranquil, content and well-pleased.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calling the fragrances of God to pass over the earth where lies one who returned to God tranquil and well-pleased; a visitation image of peace.

selected.text: Great indeed is Thy calamity and profound Thy tragedy. Were life in this first existence eternal, what Thou hast faced in Thy Lord's path would be better with God.
selected.reason: The Báb’s visitation for one of the Letters of the Living, naming the depth of his calamity in God’s path; the Báb’s voice of lament.

selected.text: News of the ascension and passing of the handmaiden of God, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting - the mother of the martyrs - has caused grief to encompass me.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grieving the passing of the mother of the martyrs; a brief lament for a woman bound to martyrdom.

selected.text: Upon thee be salutations and praise, O pride of the female kindred of that Blessed Tree whose Root is firmly established and whose Branch reacheth to the heavens!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation saluting the pride of the female kindred of the Blessed Tree; a visitation addressed to a woman of the Holy Family.

selected.text: Blessed is the earth that hath been honored by thee, and the precincts that have been ennobled by thy presence, and the air that hath been mingled with thy breath.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing the earth honored by a soul and the air mingled with his breath; a memorable image of a life’s trace.

selected.text: But the fame of the beauty of Joseph is still universal and the honor of the disciples of Christ still endures; their sufferings are the cause of life everlasting.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the fame of Joseph and the honor of Christ’s disciples endure, their sufferings the cause of life everlasting; places persecution in a long history.

selected.text: Blessed are you, then blessed are you, in this most exalted station and infinite lofty degree. Bravo, bravo to you, O sign of guidance and banner of the Most Glorious Kingdom!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation exclaiming “Bravo, bravo” to a martyr in his exalted station; a striking voice of praise.

selected.text: Praise and worship are befitting to the Lord Who made those assured souls to walk firmly in the footsteps of their noble father, so that they acquired his nature and character
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising the Lord who made a martyr’s sons walk in their father’s footsteps and acquire his character; survivors carrying a legacy.

selected.text: Then after that came news of the passing of the wise and illustrious friend, my teacher [Siyyid Kazim] - may God's mercy be upon him - from that place. And I had indeed informed some people of my dream before
selected.reason: The Báb recounting the news of the passing of His teacher Siyyid Káẓim, which He had foreseen in a dream; the Báb’s own reminiscence of a teacher.

selected.text: The peace of God, the One, the Single, be upon thee, O thou just and beloved Sovereign and noble and exalted King, and upon Muhammad and Ali and Fatima and Hassan and the Imams
selected.reason: The Báb’s visitation for the Imám Ḥusayn, invoking the peace of God upon him and the Holy Family; a visitation text in the Báb’s distinct theological voice.

selected.text: Ere long you shall observe that in the place of martyrdom, from the effect of that noble one's blood, tulips and sweet basil shall grow, and hyacinth and jasmine shall spring forth
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá foretelling that tulips, sweet basil, hyacinth and jasmine will grow where a martyr’s blood was shed; a memorable image of sacrifice bearing fruit.

selected.text: I do not know in what words I could describe my longing for my honoured sister. Whatever it may write, my pen falls short
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: May his goodly character bring honor to his lineage, and may the child prove to be the mystery of his father. For if there is no similarity in character, noble descent yields no fruit.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that a child’s goodly character honor his lineage, since noble descent without similar character yields no fruit; the guide’s key qualification on inheritance.

selected.text: Although that distinguished soul is without name or trace in this world, in the realm above his name is renowned throughout all regions, for he was a mighty pillar and a great herald.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a soul without name or trace in this world whose name is renowned in the realm above; carries the introduction’s contrast with worldly renown.

selected.text: The Beloved of Martyrs, your illustrious grandfather, was unique among martyrs and peerless among the blessed. He shines forth like the sun from the horizon of the Most Great Martyrdom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a grandson that the Beloved of Martyrs was unique among martyrs and shines like the sun; a martyr’s memory entrusted to his family.

selected.text: Mehraban Bahram has turned his face from this world and hastened to the heavenly realm, completing his work. At the time of his ascension he chanted "O Glory of God, the Most Glorious!"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Mihrabán Bahrám, who completed his work and chanted “O Glory of God, the Most Glorious!” at his ascension; a remembered final moment.

selected.text: May fragrant breezes encompass your perfumed resting place, and may clouds of forgiveness and pardon rain upon your amber-scented grave, O luminous leaf and handmaiden of the All-Merciful
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation asking that clouds of forgiveness rain upon a luminous leaf’s amber-scented grave; visitation and forgiveness for a woman.

selected.text: The days in Paris are before my eyes and cannot be forgotten. Those few days we were companions passed very pleasantly - they were sweet and full of delight, joyous and full of happiness
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling the sweet and joyous days of companionship in Paris that cannot be forgotten; remembered friendship with the living.

selected.text: We have sacrificed in the prison one of the Branches … By My life! In that station he payeth no heed to those on earth, having been seized with the intoxication of the wine of thy Lord's mercy
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that one of the Branches was sacrificed in the prison and, seized with the wine of mercy, pays no heed to those on earth; revealed words on a sacrifice in His own family.

selected.text: The glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of My mercy be upon thee and upon every servant who turned and every handmaiden who turned and remembered thy days and visited thy resting place
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh sending His glory upon every servant and handmaiden who remembers a departed woman’s days and visits her resting place; revealed blessing on visitation.

selected.text: Blessed is thy father! At the time of his ascension We perceived from him the fragrance of My love, to which the dwellers of the Most Exalted Paradise in the All-Glorious Companion bear witness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that at a father’s ascension He perceived the fragrance of His love; assurance given to a bereaved child.

selected.text: I bear witness that thou wast adorned with the love of God in thy days, in thy rising up and sitting down, and at thy ascension to a station which the tongues of the world are powerless to describe
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bearing witness that a soul was adorned with the love of God in rising and sitting and at his ascension; revealed testimony to a whole life.

selected.text: Indeed, Jamalu'd-Din, the renowned wayfarer in every clime who diffused the fragrance of the love of God, has become a wayfarer in the realms of God which are hidden from the eyes of the veiled ones.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Jamálu’d-Dín, the renowned wayfarer, who has become a wayfarer in the hidden realms of God; a traveling teacher remembered.

selected.text: When I mention thee I am reminded of that sanctified spirit, thy noble father, and how with utmost joy he drank the supreme cup of martyrdom and gave his life in the path of the Most Glorious Beauty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that mentioning a child recalls his father, who drank the cup of martyrdom with utmost joy; memory of a martyr through his child.

selected.text: Muhammad-Qabli-Rida, upon him be the light and radiance of God, dwelt for successive years beneath the shade, partaking of the fruits of the Blessed Tree and abiding beneath the pavilions of grandeur, until his days were ended by his ascension
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on Muḥammad-Qabl-i-Riḍá, who dwelt for years beneath the shade of the Blessed Tree until his ascension; a life spent in presence.

selected.text: His honor Nush found every poison (zahr) sweet (nush) and was the embodiment of reason and intelligence. He spent his days in praise of the Lord of Creation and became the cause of guidance for many.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Núsh, who found every poison sweet and became the cause of guidance for many; a memorable play on a name.

selected.text: She was very spiritual. If one were to sit and talk with her from morning to night they would not become tired. She was very unassuming and when she spoke tears would come to the eyes of her hearers
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about an unassuming woman whose speech brought tears to her hearers; a portrait of spiritual presence in conversation.

selected.text: whenever there was a gathering commemorating the martyrdom and suffering of the Lord of Martyrs, would repeatedly say with great anguish "Would that I had been with thee and attained a mighty triumph!"
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling a believer who at every commemoration of the Lord of Martyrs cried, “Would that I had been with thee”; a remembered voice of longing.

selected.text: Truly this departed one was accomplished, outspoken, articulate, calling out the appearance of God's Kingdom to both near and far. Though separation is unbearable, yet unto thy Lord is the ultimate return.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on an articulate herald of the Kingdom, admitting that separation is unbearable yet unto God is the return; grief and assurance in one sentence.

selected.text: O handmaiden of Truth! You are a memorial of Fath-i-A'zam and a descendant of that magnificent spirit. Therefore, be associated with his character and nature and be known for his qualities and attributes.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking a descendant of Fatḥ-i-A‘ẓam to be associated with his character and known for his qualities; a direct call to make inherited love visible.

selected.text: We have sat together many times before, and we shall sit together many times again in the Kingdom. We shall laugh together very much in those times, and we shall tell of the things that befell us in the Path of God
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that friends who have sat together will sit and laugh together in the Kingdom; carries the introduction’s companion remembered with laughter.

selected.text: of all worlds. By My life! From its rustling is heard: "Husayn hath attained the ultimate goal, the most exalted summit, and the Supreme Companion." Let not separation grieve thee, O Leaf, for he drinketh from the ocean of nearness and reunion, and hath attained that which cannot be mentioned in words
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a Leaf not to grieve at separation from Ḥusayn, who drinks from the ocean of nearness and reunion; revealed consolation to a bereaved woman.

selected.text: in the end their plush beds will be transformed into coarse mats and humble dust within a narrow tomb. Their names and titles will be forgotten, and their days of ease and nights of pleasure will pass away.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the plush beds of the heedless become coarse mats in a narrow tomb and their names are forgotten; the contrast that clarifies what endures.

selected.text: the luminous horizon. "Think not of those who are slain in God's way as dead. Nay, they live, finding their sustenance in the presence of their Lord." That manifest light is radiant in the ancient horizon, and that illumined candle is gleaming, shining and brilliant in the glass of the mighty Kingdom
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá citing the Qur’anic verse that those slain in God’s way are not dead but live in their Lord’s presence; scriptural assurance about martyrs.

selected.text: Lord! She was an emblem of Thy love amongst women, a firebrand set ablaze through the heat of Thy love amongst Thy handmaidens. In the dark of night, she never ceased to remember Thee in the depths of her heart.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for a woman who was an emblem of His love among women and never ceased to remember Him in the night; a woman remembered in prayer.

selected.text: in Los Angeles there is the blessed tomb of Mr. Chase. He died a few days before our arrival … I offered a supplication and chanted a Visiting Tablet. Then we scattered flowers on his Tomb and kissed its ground
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling His visit to Mr. Chase’s tomb, where He chanted a visitation, scattered flowers and kissed the ground; remembrance as an act.

selected.text: Hearts have been consumed, garments rent asunder, and wailing and lamentation have risen up, and cries of sorrow have ascended, when news of the passing of the Most Great Nabil was heard from the furthest shore.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing garments rent and cries of sorrow at news of the passing of the Most Great Nabíl; lament in its fullest form.

selected.text: Blessed is he who maketh mention of them and remembereth their remembrance and presenteth himself before their graves, saying: "I testify that ye have attained unto that which none before you have ever attained
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing whoever mentions the martyrs, remembers them and presents himself before their graves; revealed warrant for visitation.

selected.text: O Mim of Glory! Thou didst ascend with joy and fragrance, while thy loved ones remained in grief … O Ha of the Divine Essence! Thou didst seek the heights of holiness and forsake the world in the path of thy Lord
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh addressing a soul who ascended with joy while loved ones remained in grief; joy and grief named side by side.

selected.text: We wish to make mention of thy son who ascended unto Us and attained unto Our horizon and drank the choice wine of Our Revelation and immersed himself in the ocean of Our mercy which hath preceded all created things.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh making mention to a parent of a son who ascended and drank the choice wine of His Revelation; revealed consolation for a bereaved parent.

selected.text: This title is most blessed, for praise be to God that nobility of lineage has been joined with excellence of character. Those souls are children of the heart and spirit of Fath-i-A'zam, not merely children of water and clay.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that nobility of lineage has been joined with excellence of character, so these are children of Fatḥ-i-A‘ẓam’s heart and spirit, not merely of water and clay; the guide’s central statement on spiritual inheritance.

selected.text: Your noble grandfather spent his days in life serving in the path of Truth and strove with heart and soul in transcribing the Words. He possessed an illumined heart, a merciful spirit, and pure intentions in the Divine Cause.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a grandfather who strove with heart and soul in transcribing the Words; a concrete legacy of service.

selected.text: Your services in this great and accepted commemoration at the threshold of the Lord, the All-Bountiful, are most welcome. The friends should be like this, striving to honor and venerate one another, whether living or deceased.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá welcoming a commemoration and asking the friends to honor and venerate one another, whether living or deceased; states the practice of remembrance itself.

selected.text: Mirza Ahmad Qa'ini, that luminous figure and divine soul, during the height of war between nations and peoples, reached the shore of the Holy Land with utmost difficulty. Since the routes were blocked, he stayed at the Holy Threshold and, with complete attraction and enthusiasm, arose to tend the Holy Garden. He had no rest day or night
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Mírzá Aḥmad Qá’iní, who reached the Holy Land in wartime and tended the Holy Garden day and night; a distinctive practical service.

selected.text: Lua was heavenly, divine, merciful, attracted to the divine fragrances. That blessed leaf became the cause of guidance for many, for she had an attracted heart and an eloquent tongue and was occupied with teaching day and night.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Lua, whose attracted heart and eloquent tongue made her the cause of guidance for many; a woman teacher remembered.

selected.text: Now that pure spirit has ascended to the Abha Kingdom, that dove has taken flight to the realm of immortality, and that moth has soared around the lamp of the Supreme Concourse. Thus his place in this lower world remains empty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a pure spirit has taken flight to immortality while his place in this lower world remains empty; holds assurance and absence together.

selected.text: Indeed in the rose-garden of God that young man was like unto a shrub in its utmost freshness and promising good fruits.  Whoever has seen him or heard him has undoubtedly been shocked and grieved at the news of his passing away
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá picturing a young man as a fresh shrub in the rose-garden of God whose passing shocked all who knew him; youthful loss lamented.

selected.text: Without doubt you are the shell that contains the hidden pearl and treasured gem, who nurtured that brilliant pearl in your embrace through the spring rains. Therefore you are infinitely respected in the presence of 'Abdu'l-Baha
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá honoring a mother as the shell that nurtured the hidden pearl of her child; respect for a bereaved parent.

selected.text: Concerning the holy, fragrant, and luminous resting-place of the illustrious wife--my soul yearneth to inhale the holy savour of its dust--it must be cared for with the utmost respect until the time cometh when it shall be exalted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directing that the resting-place of an illustrious wife be cared for with utmost respect; carries the arc’s care of graves.

selected.text: That family has been divine from the Day of Alast - they took up the cup of the love of God, drank from it and gave others to drink … All of this is due to the blessing of the sincerity of the respected grandfather and noble father
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a family that drank the cup of the love of God and gave others to drink, through the sincerity of grandfather and father; a family legacy.

selected.text: When that blessed name was read, such a state overtook me that I involuntarily began writing a reply, although I had absolutely no time. This is due to the blessing of the blessed name of that martyr in the path of the Beauty of Abha.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing how reading a martyr’s name moved Him to write a reply despite having no time; remembrance overtaking the writer.

selected.text: The passing of his honor Adib and the ascension of that beloved one caused intense grief. Show much love and kindness to the survivors of that illustrious person. Console them. Soon prayers and a visitation tablet will be sent for him.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the passing of Adíb, asking that much love be shown to his survivors and that they be consoled; care for those who remain.

selected.text: Walk thou in the footsteps of thy father, for he witnessed such evidences from thy Creator and beheld such signs from thy Lord as no eye hath ever seen, and attained that which hath shone forth from this holy, mighty and wondrous Scene.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a child to walk in the footsteps of his father, who beheld signs no eye had seen; revealed counsel on inheritance.

selected.text: Gudarz the Persian was asleep and awakened, was unconscious and became conscious … He was God-seeking, God-speaking, of goodly character and radiant countenance, until he went to Qazvin and became intimate and confidant with the friends
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Gúdarz the Persian, who was asleep and awakened, became God-seeking and an intimate of the friends in Qazvín; a life of awakening.

selected.text: The deceased, his honor Mr. Chase, was a blessed soul; he was a holy reality. His station in this life was not known. Yesterday I took a special trip and visited his tomb. At the time of visiting his tomb I found wonderful spirituality.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Mr. Chase’s station was not known in this life and that at his tomb He found wonderful spirituality; a grave visited.

selected.text: His Honor Aga Reza and His Honor Aga Mahmoud were most sincere. They were serving day and night. in reality they accomplished such services that cannot be duplicated by another human being, viz;- it is beyond the power of human endurance
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Áqá Riḍá and Áqá Maḥmúd served day and night beyond the power of human endurance; remembered companions in service.

selected.text: O My handmaiden and My leaf! Thou hast been mentioned in the presence of the Wronged One and hast not been forgotten. Today the glance of loving-kindness hath been directed toward the steadfast handmaidens of God, and will continue to be so.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assuring a handmaiden that she has been mentioned before the Wronged One and has not been forgotten; revealed assurance of remembrance.

selected.text: We have remembered thy father with a remembrance whereby the Concourse on High and they who circle round My mighty Throne do remember him, and We have adorned him with the ornament of forgiveness as a bounty from thy Lord, the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh remembering a father with the remembrance of the Concourse on High and adorning him with forgiveness; revealed assurance to a family.

selected.text: O son of Nabil who ascended to the Kingdom of his Glorious Lord! May God assist you in all things and make you a brilliant sign and a radiant star in the horizon of possibility. Ask God that you may be a worthy memorial to that noble father
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that the son of Nabíl become a radiant star and asking him to be a worthy memorial to his father; the obligation of a living memorial.

selected.text: Indeed, he sacrificed his soul for Prague and offered his body as an oblation for the friends. That pure and holy soul ascended to the luminous Kingdom, that spotless spirit passed beyond the spheres and became radiant in the eternal world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a believer who sacrificed his soul for Prague and offered his body for the friends; a distinctive sacrifice remembered.

selected.text: O unique, peerless, and glorious martyr! I salute your pure dust and your holy, blessed, and fragrant resting place through the holy breaths that waft over you from the Supreme Concourse and the lights that fall upon you from the Abha Kingdom
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation for Áqá Siyyid Ja‘far, saluting the pure dust and fragrant resting place of the peerless martyr; visitation at a martyr’s grave.

selected.text: Verily, Thy servant ‘Ali-Akbar hath believed in Thee and in Thy Signs; hath acknowledged Thine omnipotence and Thy sovereignty; hath been attracted by the fragrance of Thy sweet savours; hath become enkindled by the fire of Thy love, even whilst in the flower of life and the flush of youth
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O thou whom God hath aided to follow in the footsteps of thy glorious uncle and unique and peerless ancestor! 'Abdu'l-Baha's utmost desire is that that illustrious family may become radiant and that lineage may become the dawning-place of lights.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising one aided to follow in the footsteps of an uncle and ancestor, hoping the family becomes a dawning-place of lights; kinship as a call to conduct.

selected.text: The Supreme Pen makes mention of the people of that household. By My life! The departed and blessed one who was named Muhammad-'Ali, upon him be My glory and mercy, and those related to him have ever been and are remembered in the Most Holy Court.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that the departed Muḥammad-‘Alí and his household are remembered in the Most Holy Court; remembrance extended to a family.

selected.text: O loved ones of God! Praise be to God that those pure souls were freed from the dusty world and joined the angels of the celestial realm, meaning they acquired heavenly attributes and found their way to the private chamber of the All-Merciful Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that departed souls joining the angels means they acquired heavenly attributes; a necessary qualification on the imagery of the next life.

selected.text: I testify that you showed patience in tribulation, remained steadfast in hardship and trials, drank the cup of cruelty, and became the target of arrows of accusations in those regions - all out of passionate love for God, seeking God's good pleasure
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation for the mother of Ibn-i-Abhar, testifying to her patience under cruelty and accusation; a woman’s endurance under persecution.

selected.text: You are the memento of that illustrious martyr - how could I forget? Whenever I write to you, I remember that noble soul and become extremely affected. Indeed, most times while writing letters, such longing overcomes me that my eyes fill with tears.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a martyr’s relative that writing to him brings such longing that His eyes fill with tears; carries the guide’s voice of grief.

selected.text: Praise be to God, you have traversed a great distance, reached the intended destination, arrived at the Ka'bah of existence, entered the Most Remote Temple, circled the sacred precincts of the Most Great, and perfumed your nostrils with the holy dust.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a pilgrim who traversed a great distance and perfumed his nostrils with the holy dust; opens the section on journeys.

selected.text: In mourning and lamentation for his holiness the Afnan of the Divine Lote-Tree, his honor Aqa Siyyid Mirza, you have spoken words and penned an elegy, giving full measure of eloquence and rhetoric. It was most novel and elegant, touching wounded hearts.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising an elegy penned for the Afnán Áqá Siyyid Mírzá as touching wounded hearts; carries the arc’s composing of poetry.

selected.text: O first light that shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of the loving-kindness of the Lord of all beings, and first word uttered by the Tongue of Grandeur, and first fragrance that wafted from the garment of My Most Great Name amongst the nations!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s visitation for Zahrá Bagum, hailing her as the first light and first fragrance from the garment of His Name; a revealed visitation for a woman of the Holy Family.

selected.text: Blessed is he who remembereth thy days and through thee draweth nigh unto God, thy Lord, the Lord of all who are in the heavens and on earth. O Salih, forget not thy loved ones in thy glorious station and thy blessed, exalted and manifest dwelling-place.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá blessing whoever remembers Ṣáliḥ’s days and asking him not to forget his loved ones from his exalted station; mutual remembrance across death.

selected.text: God, I am none other than the soul of Ali among you, and the spirit of Muhammad within you, and the beauty of God before you! Fear ye God, and be not of the wrongdoers! Fear God, and shed not the blood through which the pillars of the Throne are shaken, and the foundations of Paradise do tremble, and the hearts of them that are nigh unto God are consumed
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning, “Fear God, and shed not the blood” through which the pillars of the Throne are shaken; the texts’ strong language addressed to persecutors.

selected.text: O ye who remain of that orb which dawned in the horizon of the Kingdom of Abha! … Whenever I write to any one of you, my spirit becomes fragrant and my soul and consciousness are filled with honey and sugar, for mention of that embodied spirit flows from my pen
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that whenever He writes to the remnants of a departed soul His spirit becomes fragrant with the mention of him; remembrance as joy.

selected.text: O ye who are related to him who hath attained the presence of the Glorious Companion! … Although that well-favored one at the threshold of Grandeur hath hastened unto the precincts of unsurpassed mercy, he hath left you as a heritage to each of the friends of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to the relatives of a departed believer that he has left them as a heritage to each of the friends of God; entrusts survivors to the community.

selected.text: His Holiness Minshadi was in truth a resplendent garden whose sweet fragrance was diffused throughout the East and the West. Now that garden hath been transported to the eternal realm, that its sweet perfume may make fragrant the nostrils of the spiritual world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá picturing Manshádí as a garden whose fragrance spread East and West and is now transported to the eternal realm; a memorable image of continuing influence.

selected.text: O Zaynu'l-'Abidin! The Lord of the worlds maketh mention of thee from the Most Great Scene, that this mention may be a companion unto thee, a light unto thee, a glory unto thee, an honor unto thee, and a treasure unto thee in every world of the worlds of thy Lord.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling Zaynu’l-‘Ábidín that His mention will be a companion, light and treasure to him in every world; remembrance as companionship beyond death.

selected.text: Your noble brother has traversed the realm of possibility … He never rested, never drew an easy breath, never sought comfort, never found repose, never settled down … until he ascended to the horizon of glory and became the object of praise of the Concourse on High
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a brother who never rested, never sought comfort, until he ascended and was praised by the Concourse on High; a tireless life remembered to his family.

selected.text: Marzuban has abandoned the earthly realm and hastened to the boundless world. He had no hope except in You and planted nothing in the field of his heart except the seeds of Your love. He grew weary of life in the world of dust and soared to the Kingdom of mysteries.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for Marzubán, who planted nothing in his heart but the seeds of God’s love and soared to the Kingdom; a brief prayer for the departed.

selected.text: A tribulation has struck that has demolished the edifice of patience and has laid waste the towers of joy … O regret that the mighty pillar has fallen, the glorious banner has been reversed, the lofty sail has been furled, and the fires of joy have been extinguished
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a tribulation that demolished the edifice of patience, the mighty pillar fallen and the banner reversed; a lament in sustained images.

selected.text: Such was his condition, when he died. Many and many a time, Baha'u'llah was heard to express His satisfaction with Ustad Isma'il. Blessings hemmed him round, and the eye of God was on him. Salutations be unto him, and praise. Upon him be the glory of the All-Glorious.
selected.reason: Memorials of the Faithful recalling that Bahá’u’lláh often expressed His satisfaction with Ustád Ismá‘íl, on whom the eye of God rested; a closing benediction from that work.

selected.text: Rif'at was clever, this young child was the lamp of the gathering and the sweet-singing bird of that dwelling. She would recite the verses and chant the words with the most wondrous melodies. She was like an articulate nightingale, in harmony with the Concourse on High.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the young child Rif‘at, the lamp of the gathering, who chanted the verses like an articulate nightingale; a child remembered tenderly.

selected.text: He had a living heart and a becoming form. His countenance was moon-like and his nature musk-scented. He was a sapling of utmost freshness and delicacy, with a sweet appearance. His heart was enamored with the Heavenly Beloved and his soul yearned for the divine Kingdom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a youth of moon-like countenance and musk-scented nature whose heart yearned for the Kingdom; a young life portrayed in grief.

selected.text: O descendants of His Holiness Mawzun and Siraju'sh-Shuhada, those two precious souls are alive through the breath of the All-Merciful and are intimate companions. In the Kingdom of holiness they chant the verses of the supreme gift and encourage you to follow their example
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to descendants of Mawzún and Siráju’sh-Shuhadá that the two souls are alive in the Kingdom and encourage them to follow their example; the departed as living example.

selected.text: For his holiness Vahid hath this been revealed, he who beheld the Countenance of God, the All-Glorious, the Almighty, and who in His path sacrificed himself, arose to serve His Cause and quaffed his fill of the draught of certitude from the Hand of his Lord, the Munificent.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s visitation for Vaḥíd, who beheld the Countenance of God and sacrificed himself in His path; a revealed martyr’s visitation.

selected.text: That bountiful grove, verdant garden, and fragrant bower adorned with Divine good-pleasure hath ascended unto the Kingdom of Abha. With the rose, myrtle, hyacinth, and jasmine of perfections, he was a sublime heaven and a lofty, light-giving paradise of the Luminous Horizon.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá picturing a departed soul as a bountiful grove and fragrant bower adorned with the rose, myrtle, hyacinth and jasmine of perfections; a garden image echoing the opening.

selected.text: He arose to guide humanity, healed the deaf, the dumb and the blind, and brought the dead to life through the spirit of guidance. He served Thy Most Exalted Threshold through the confirmation of the All-Powerful One. He spoke in praise and called to Thy Most Supreme Kingdom.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for one who arose to guide humanity and brought the dead to life through the spirit of guidance; service described in its spiritual effect.

selected.text: O sign of steadfastness and banner of firmness, Mirza Taraz! Praise be to God, he is harmonious and in tune. Like the spiritual spring breeze, he traversed every region and territory of Iran and gave new life to souls. Now he has reached the proximity of the Forgiving Lord
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Mírzá Ṭaráz, who like a spring breeze traversed every region of Iran and gave new life to souls; a traveling teacher in a short prayer-like tribute.

selected.text: Know ye the station of your father, for he is among those who emigrated unto God and attained His presence and heard His most wondrous, most beautiful, mighty and invincible call, and succeeded in serving the Cause in His days when every distant misbeliever turned away from it
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding children know the station of their father, who emigrated to God and served when others turned away; revealed praise of a parent.

selected.text: Then the Blessed Beauty summoned me and asked why I was not writing to him. "Write to him." So I wrote him a reply with this meaning: "O honorable Varqa, have you not heard the call of the Supreme Concourse? Then why are you waiting and expecting the sound of a mosquito?" etc.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling Bahá’u’lláh’s instruction to write to Varqá and the reply asking why he awaits the sound of a mosquito; a memorable exchange.

selected.text: O honored cousin, precious memento of that embodied spirit and that manifest light, my revered uncle! He was infinitely kind to Abdul-Baha. In the days of childhood when I was in that village he showed much affection and association. The sweetness of his love is still in my taste.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling a revered uncle’s affection in his childhood, whose sweetness is still in his taste; a vivid sensory memory of kinship.

selected.text: Verily, those near unto God wandered through deserts and wilderness, mountains and valleys, seeking fragments of your bodies that perchance they might inhale from them the fragrance of the love of God, your Creator, your Beloved, your Goal, your Worshipped One, and your Quickener.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing those near to God wandering deserts and mountains seeking fragments of the martyrs’ bodies; the survivors’ voice in its strongest language.

selected.text: Today a most painful news was received; its effect was agonizing and its anguish very harrowing. Truly I say Mirza Abu'l-Fadl was a glorious personage. From every standpoint he was peerless. It is a rare thing to find a person perfect from every direction, but he was such a person.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the painful news of Mírzá Abu’l-Faḍl’s death, calling him peerless and perfect from every standpoint; sets the opening note of loss.

selected.text: He was truly a great personage - noble and distinguished, eminent and excellent. He was an expounder of proofs and evidences, and an establisher of divine arguments and demonstrations. He trained children who today are distinguished, independent, and intimate with divine mysteries.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on an expounder of proofs who trained children now distinguished and intimate with divine mysteries; service carried forward in a family.

selected.text: When I look at you, I see in you the joy of the loved ones who attained the Supreme Companion, His Holiness Aqa Siyyid 'Ali, and the essence of faithfulness who entered the Most Glorious Kingdom, Aqa Ghulam-Husayn Khan, and I smell from you the sweet and fragrant breaths of their love.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that in a believer He sees the joy of departed loved ones and smells the fragrance of their love; the presence of the departed in the living.

selected.text: We have deposited his luminous remains in a land called Izmir. Verily it is God's trust in that blessed and wondrous spot. Blessed is he who draweth nigh unto it and visiteth it with that which hath been revealed from the Pen of his Lord's Revelation, the All-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that a believer’s luminous remains were laid in Izmir as God’s trust and blessing whoever visits that spot; a grave on the road.

selected.text: O you who are a remembrance of that brilliant star! … Now that you have reached that region and picked flowers and herbs from that garden of love, you must hasten to Bukhara on behalf of 'Abdu'l-Baha and visit the fragrant shrine of His Holiness the learned Nabil, upon him be the Glory of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking a traveler to hasten to Bukhárá on His behalf to visit the shrine of the learned Nabíl; a journey undertaken for remembrance.

selected.text: the day he passed away. I became very sorrowful and grieved at his passing, for he was my companion, my comfort and intimate friend. Know the worth of this uncle. This respected soul is near in the Divine Court and immersed in the ocean of lights in the world of mysteries. His worth is not known now but soon it will become known. This noble person placed a crown upon your heads whose brilliant and radiant jewels will shine throughout centuries and ages
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grieving an uncle who was his companion and comfort, whose worth is not yet known but will become known; links personal loss with lasting legacy.

selected.text: of the Tree of Holiness! Though that illustrious offshoot was severed from the garden of the contingent world, he hath been joined to the sacred Lote-Tree and hath grown fresh and verdant in the garden of the Placeless. He hath been nurtured from the wellspring of living waters and stirred by the breezes wafting from the bowers of the Abha Kingdom. He hath entered the paradise of the Divine
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Then rejoice within thyself that thy father hath attained unto the presence of God and his spirit hath ascended to a station whereof the knowledge of the knowers is cut off. The maidens of Paradise shall now serve him and the denizens of the Supreme Concourse shall find solace in his company.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a child rejoice that his father has attained the presence of God and that the Concourse finds solace in his company; closes the guide in revealed assurance.

selected.text: During his lifetime he arose to serve those near the Divine Threshold and was confirmed in servitude at the Sacred Court. You who are the honored spouse of that pure soul should live according to his way and conduct so that you may become the cause of his joy and delight in the eternal world.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking the spouse of a departed servant to live according to his way so as to be the cause of his joy in the eternal world; conduct as the response to loss.

selected.text: O Ali, verily We made mention of thee before, and We make mention of My handmaiden who hath ascended to the Most Glorious Horizon and the Supreme Companion. We make mention of her with a remembrance whose fragrance shall endure as long as My most beautiful names and supreme attributes endure.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh making mention of a departed handmaiden with a remembrance whose fragrance shall endure as long as His names endure; enduring remembrance.

selected.text: Thy noble father was a lamp of light and one near to the threshold of the Lord. He was constant in service and perpetual in servitude. He was Ghulam-Husayn, renowned throughout East and West. The Blessed Beauty was well-pleased with him, and he was the object of praise of the Concourse on High.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Ghulám-Ḥusayn, constant in service and renowned East and West, with whom the Blessed Beauty was well-pleased; a father remembered to his child.

selected.text: Grieve not for thy father. He hath quaffed the choice wine of reunion and found intimacy with Him when he was in the land of Ta. Thy Lord is verily the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. Be thou assured that he hath ascended unto God and attained what was ordained for him in My most exalted Kingdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling a child to grieve not for his father, who has quaffed the wine of reunion; revealed consolation.

selected.text: This is a day wherein the Tree of Utterance hath spoken at the heart of creation concerning that which hath appeared in the realm of origination and that which hath befallen its branches. Sorrows have encompassed Me by reason of your grief, as witnessed by the Divine Lote-Tree and its branches.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that sorrows have encompassed Him by reason of the grief of those afflicted; revealed sharing in the survivors’ grief.

selected.text: to pay you a visit. I was exceedingly sad and heart-broken when I heard of the departure of Mr. Chase, for I loved him very much. He was a near soul to God. Mr. Chase was a man who will never be forgotten. His value is not now known, but will be in the future. Throughout the Orient his name was well known and they all longed to see
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to Mrs. Chase on His grief, saying her husband will never be forgotten and his value will be known; consolation given in person.

selected.text: and glory be upon thee, O blessed Leaf sprung from the Lote-Tree! I bear witness that thou didst believe in God and in His signs, didst respond to His call, didst turn unto Him, didst hold fast to His cord, didst cling to the hem of His bounty, didst emigrate in His path, and didst choose for thyself a lonely resting-place in a strange land, out of love for meeting Him and longing to serve
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing a Leaf who emigrated in His path and chose a lonely resting-place in a strange land; a woman’s exile and devotion.

selected.text: The splendor of God rest upon you, O Dayspring of faithfulness from God, Creator of heaven! … I testify that through you the city of servitude was adorned, its banners were raised, its gates were decorated, and its birds sang. I testify that you turned to God and voiced His praise among His servants
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s visitation hailing a Dayspring of faithfulness through whom the city of servitude was adorned; revealed visitation praise.

selected.text: the Call of the Lord! O nostrils invigorated by inhaling the pure breath of the Guidance of God ! O palates refreshed by tasting every bitterness yet sweetened in the path of the Love of God! May my spirit be a sacrifice for you! May my being be a sacrifice for you ! May my reality be a sacrifice for you! O brilliant faces! O heavenly souls! O celestial severed heads! O orbs of oneness! O divine soldiers! Blessed are ye! Well done! Glory be upon
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s salutation to the martyrs as brilliant faces and celestial severed heads, “Blessed are ye! Well done!”; prayer at its most intense.

selected.text: He was clear-sighted, for he was confirmed in service at the Sacred Threshold and assisted in servitude at the Court of Oneness. He was firm and steadfast in the Covenant and Testament of the All-Merciful, and until his final breath and ascension he remained stable and upright like a mountain of iron.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a believer who remained upright like a mountain of iron in the Covenant until his final breath; a strong image of steadfastness.

selected.text: O descendant of Abraham! Truly you are from the family of that noble one and from the lineage of that radiant sun. The musk-scented fragrance of Khalil's nature emanates from the garment of your character, and the brilliant signs of Abrahamic inheritance are evident in your steadfastness and firmness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá telling a descendant of Abraham that the signs of his Abrahamic inheritance are evident in his steadfastness; inheritance shown in character.

selected.text: He was a tree bearing fruits, and a Lote-Tree bearing praise and remembrance. … O My loved ones in Taft! Recognize the exalted station and make mention of it through that which hath been sent down from My Most Exalted Pen. Blessed is he who loved him and made mention of him before and after his ascension
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling a departed believer a tree bearing fruits and blessing whoever loved him and mentioned him before and after his ascension; revealed warrant for remembrance.

selected.text: During successive years she circled around the court of her Lord, and lauded Him in her anthems of praise, both in verse and prose, for which she gained the ornament of His acceptance, and received the light of His divine good-pleasure, as a token of heavenly grace from God, the Lord of this wondrous Day.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on a woman who for years lauded Him in verse and prose and gained His acceptance; revealed praise for a writer’s devotion.

selected.text: That bird of the meadow of guidance hath hastened to the rose-garden of reality, and he hath left these companions as his heritage that after his return to the divine homeland, ye might irrigate the field he hath sown, arrange the flowers of true understanding in the boulevard of his hopes and aspirations
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a departed believer left his companions as heritage to irrigate the field he sowed; legacy as continuing work.

selected.text: I swear by the Sun of Truth that thy mention hath been inscribed in God's Book by the Most Glorious Pen, and thou art remembered before the Concourse on High and the dwellers of the Most Exalted Paradise, for thou didst witness and hear in His path what the devoted women of former ages witnessed and heard.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh swearing that a woman’s mention is inscribed in God’s Book, for she witnessed what devoted women of former ages witnessed; links remembered women across history.

selected.text: Consider how much 'Abdu'l-Baha cherishes the faithfulness of your illustrious father in the path of the Gracious Lord. He endured every affliction and trial, drank deadly poison as though it were pure water, diffused the divine fragrances, and finally passed away to the sanctified Kingdom in sorrowful exile.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a father who drank deadly poison as though it were pure water and passed away in sorrowful exile; faithfulness remembered for his child.

selected.text: Truly both nobility of lineage and excellence of character are combined in you, and you are descended from the spiritual essence of that one ascended unto God, and emerged from his earthly nature. For you have taken up his path and found his way, and "the son is the secret of his father" has become manifest.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a descendant combines lineage with character by taking up his father’s path, so that “the son is the secret of his father”; inheritance through conduct.

selected.text: News arrived from the palace that Aqa Baji has ascended from this mortal dust heap to the eternal heights of glory. After enduring eighty years of hardship and attaining to service, in her final days she escaped from the difficulties of physical realms and pitched her tent in the rose garden of divine mercy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Áqá Bájí, who after eighty years of hardship and service pitched her tent in the rose garden of divine mercy; a long life of a woman remembered.

selected.text: O servant! Rejoice within thyself that thou wast confirmed in the good-pleasure of God and the recognition of His Self, and wast content with His good-pleasure until thou didst sacrifice thy spirit in His path. And verily We were with thee when thou didst ascend unto God with manifest humility and submission.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding a martyred servant rejoice and testifying that He was with him when he ascended in humility; revealed nearness at a martyr’s death.

selected.text: This glorious soul [Mirza 'Abu'l-Fadl] was a luminous star, a bright lamp, a blessed and fruitful tree, a billowing ocean of knowledge, a fountain of everlasting life, and well-established in the Ark of Salvation. From the beginning of his childhood, he lived a life of utmost piety and spent all his days in acquiring perfections
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing Abu’l-Faḍl as a luminous star and billowing ocean of knowledge who lived in piety from childhood; opens the section on learning.

selected.text: His honor "he who attained the presence of his Lord," Jinab-i-Muntaha Aqa Mirza Mahdi, the pure brother, truly arose as he should to servitude and became the cause of exalting the Word of God in all regions. Like a life-giving breeze he traveled everywhere, was a divine herald and bearer of infinite bounties.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Mírzá Mahdí, the pure brother, who traveled everywhere like a life-giving breeze as a divine herald; sustained service on the road.

selected.text: As Shah-Siyavush was like an angel and a divine messenger, a devoted servant at the threshold of the Most Glorious Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones - therefore, after his ascension he became a guardian at the threshold of the Most Glorious Kingdom and was numbered among the true servants.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Sháh-Siyávush, a devoted servant at the threshold, became after his ascension a guardian at the threshold of the Kingdom; continuity of service beyond death.

selected.text: To be brief: I hope her noble son may seek the Path wherein his mother walked, and may become better and more illustrious; nay, rather, the lights of his love may also take effect in his grand parents
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hoping a noble son may walk the Path his mother walked and that his love may reach his grandparents; legacy passing through a mother.

selected.text: May greetings of mercy and good-pleasure be upon your radiant dust, your white spot, your purified grave and your illumined tomb, O namesake of Glory, concealed in devotion, manifest in faithfulness, trusted one of the chosen ones, pillar of the pious ones, exemplar of martyrs and support of the people of sacrifice
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation for Shaykh Ḥusayn Mu‘tamidu’sh-Sharí‘ih, greeting his radiant dust and calling him exemplar of martyrs; a martyr’s visitation in its own source.

selected.text: Abu'l-Fadl served humanity until his last breath and laid a foundation that will endure forever. A thousand regrets that this bright candle was outwardly extinguished, but it was illumined in the gathering of the supreme realm. And praise be to God that he left behind traces that will radiate light forever and ever.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Abu’l-Faḍl served humanity to his last breath and left traces that will radiate light forever; the enduring record of a life.

selected.text: We make mention of thy father, through whom the lips of mystical knowledge smiled in all creation and who attained the presence of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. We make mention of him with that which nothing on earth can equal, and We remember him throughout the duration of the kingdom and the heavenly kingdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on a father through whom the lips of mystical knowledge smiled and whom He remembers throughout the kingdom; revealed remembrance.

selected.text: Indeed that respected person served the Word of God and endured many hardships. His services in the Kingdom of God are recorded in the eternal ledger and are mentioned in the Supreme Concourse. They will never be forgotten. Soon they will yield magnificent results and become the cause of joy and honor for that family.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that a servant’s hardships and services are recorded in the eternal ledger and will bring honor to his family; consolation that looks to the survivors.

selected.text: who art a relative of a servant who hath attained the greatest gift of grace and bounty! O handmaiden of God, be thou glad and smile through the favor of thy Lord, inasmuch as He created thee from a father who believed in God and His signs, who was attracted by His fragrances, who stood firm in His Covenant, who hastened to His holy court, who circumambulated the sanctuary of the company of those near unto God, and who pressed his brow and face against the dust of His divine threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bidding a handmaiden be glad and smile because she was created from a father who believed and stood firm; joy in inherited faith.

selected.text: May the shining light and brilliant radiance from the Supreme Horizon envelop the soil that contains your pure and purified grave … The eyes of the people of the Most Glorious Kingdom have wept, and tears have flowed from the eyelids of the people of the exalted scenes of grandeur upon the fragrant soil of your shrine
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation saying the people of the Kingdom have wept upon the fragrant soil of a shrine; lament at a resting place.

selected.text: Your distinguished father has taken flight to the Kingdom of lights. However, after perfecting his servitude at the Threshold of the Lord and enduring boundless troubles and hardships, praise be to God, he possessed such conduct, speech and deeds that he was the envy of the righteous and the object of jealousy to strangers.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a father whose conduct, speech and deeds after boundless hardship made him the envy of the righteous; legacy as character.

selected.text: That distinguished martyr, like unto a lucky star, shineth from the dawning-place of divine unity, luminous, resplendent and unmistakable, though mortal eyes are debarred from beholding him. With his face beaming with light, with a luminous brow and enthralling beauty, he is calling aloud from the summit of the heaven of glory
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Truly, Mr. Chase was a glorious personage, having no desire save the good pleasure of God. His attention was directed to the Kingdom of God. He served during his lifetime. He was not at all wanting in service. He compiled certain books proving the validity of the Movement. As much as he could, he endeavored to guide the people.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that Mr. Chase served throughout his life and compiled books proving the validity of the Cause; the written record of a life.

selected.text: We testify that she attained the presence of God and heard the call of her Lord when the Desired One was seated upon the throne of His mercy that hath encompassed all who are in the heavens and on earth. Grieve not for her - verily she hath ascended unto the Sadratu'l-Muntaha, the Most Exalted Horizon, and the Supreme Companion.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the bereaved grieve not for a woman who attained His presence and has ascended to the Most Exalted Horizon; revealed consolation.

selected.text: The Most Exalted Leaf of Paradise, upon her be the Glory of God the Most Glorious, was a manifestation of the supreme bounty and the recipient of endless favors. From the dawning of the Morn of Guidance and the rising of the Most Exalted Sun, she was attracted to the holy fragrances and enkindled with the fire of the love of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the Most Exalted Leaf of Paradise, enkindled with the love of God from the dawning of the Morn of Guidance; a woman remembered for early faith.

selected.text: I testify that you believed in God and were certain of God's verses and submitted to the Manifestation of God's lights and were humble before the Dawning Place of God's revelation and were attracted by the fragrances of God and protected the Dayspring of God's light and preserved the Center of Guidance from the evil of the enemies
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s visitation for Manúchihr Khán, testifying that he protected the Dayspring of God’s light from the enemies; a visitation recalling a historic protection.

selected.text: He was truly a blessed being and sincere in the Cause of Truth. During this time nothing was heard about him except praise and commendation. He was always engaged in his work with a detached heart, a joyous spirit and a breast dilated through divine favors. He was a calm being, content with his state, thankful, grateful and happy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a calm, contented believer who worked with a detached heart and a joyous spirit; quiet virtue remembered.

selected.text: With tearful eyes and burning heart you lamented and cried out over the ascension of your kind father. You are right to do so, it is fitting, for a loving father is most precious, especially one who lit the candle with the fire of the love of God and, like a moth, consumed his soul circling around the lamp of the Supreme Concourse.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá affirming that a child’s tearful lament for a loving father is right and fitting; the guide’s clearest permission for grief.

selected.text: Although they have sacrificed their heads in the world of dust, they have raised them in the world of sanctity. Though they have spilled their pure blood upon the dusty earth, they have clung to the hem of grandeur in the kingdom of the Most Glorious and sweetened the cup of martyrdom at the banquet of reunion with nectar and sugar.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the martyrs sacrificed their heads in the world of dust and raised them in the world of sanctity; a memorable reversal image.

selected.text: When we were in Bagdad there was amongst the believers a young man by the name of Janabé Moneab. He was one of the most spiritual youths that I have known in the Baha'i revelation. He possessed a sweet, affable temper and a pure, sterling character. I was greatly attached to him and from the depth of my heart I admired and loved him.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling Janabé Moneab in Baghdad, a youth of sweet temper and sterling character whom He loved; affection remembered across decades.

selected.text: There was a Mohamad Bey, a Kurd, of short stature, fat and a long beard. He had met Baha'u'llah when he was living in the mountain of Soleymanieh and became His ardent follower. When Baha'u'llah returned from the mountains after two years of absence, this Mohamad Bey also came to Bagdad bringing 46 mares for the governor Omar pasha.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the Kurdish follower Mohamad Bey, short and bearded, who brought forty-six mares to Baghdad; a vivid, humorous particular.

selected.text: O My Most Exalted Pen! Make mention of him who heard My call, held fast to My cord, and uttered My praise. He is indeed of the people of Baha and the companions of the Crimson Ark. Say: The first light that dawned from the horizon of the Most Merciful's utterance and the first fragrance that wafted in the days of God, the Lord of all beings - upon thee, O thou who didst attain unto faith when the people were wrapped in the darkness of vain imaginings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh commanding the Pen to mention one who attained faith when the people were wrapped in vain imaginings; revealed praise of early recognition.

selected.text: The death of Sa'd was not the death of one alone, … But rather was the collapse of a people's edifice." … That bird of fidelity soared to the rose garden of eternity, that moth was consumed by the divine flame, that yearning soul hastened to the assemblage of the Day Star of all horizons, and that fish found its way to the limitless ocean
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the death of Sa‘d was the collapse of a people’s edifice, then picturing the soul as a bird, moth and fish reaching the ocean; a memorable image of loss and release.

selected.text: He was in truth, an embodiment of spirituality and an image of light. Whenever his radiant countenance is called to mind I feel a divine happiness. The splendors of truthfulness, love of God and knowledge of God emanated from his effulgent and luminous brow. His resignation and submission unto the Will of God was evident and manifest.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that whenever a martyr’s radiant countenance comes to mind He feels divine happiness, recalling his resignation to God’s Will; remembrance as joy amid persecution.

selected.text: The love which 'Abdu'l-Baha beareth for the survivors of the martyrs is to the degree that the Concourse on high applaud it! These blessed souls laid down their lives. To use the popular expression, "It is no laughing matter." They tasted the venom of the sword, and made their mirror-like breasts the targets of a hundred thousand arrows
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on His love for the survivors of the martyrs, who “tasted the venom of the sword”; care for families of the persecuted.

selected.text: for that precious soul who was the comfort of every dear one and the cause of joy to the hearts of rich and poor alike, has vanished like a luminous star behind the clouds of absence. The candle of the gathering has been extinguished, and from the intensity of pain and grief, it has caused tumult in the hearts and souls of the friends.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that the candle of the gathering is extinguished and the hearts of the friends are in tumult; communal grief.

selected.text: This servant remembers Thy servant who was ever the recipient of the glances of Thine eye of mercy and the object of the gaze of Thy loving-kindness among Thy creatures. He was ever a servant of Thy Cause, a spreader of Thy remembrance, a counselor to Thy creation, a guide to Thy servants, a herald of Thy name, and a servant at Thy gate
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá remembering a servant who was a counselor to creation, a guide to God’s servants and a herald of His name; a prayer that names a life’s roles.

selected.text: His Holiness Abu'l-Fadl, may my spirit be sacrificed for him, did not rest for a moment during his life, nor did he find comfort on any pillow at night. Day and night he engaged in promoting the Cause of God and exalting the Word of God, establishing proofs and evidence, and writing responses to the objections of every sinful falsifier.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Abu’l-Faḍl, who never rested day or night from establishing proofs and writing responses to objections; scholarship as service.

selected.text: Reflect upon Abu-Basir and Ashraf and that which was manifested from them … Blessed are they both, and blessed is he who visiteth them, who seeketh them out, who turneth toward them, who maketh mention of them, and who draweth nigh through them unto God, the Forgiving, the Generous. … With illumined hearts and radiant faces did they ascend
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on Abú-Baṣír and Ashraf, who ascended with radiant faces, and the blessing on whoever visits and mentions them; martyrs remembered by name.

selected.text: O 'Ali! Thou art in the highest Paradise while the Wronged One remembereth thee in the prison of 'Akka, and remembereth the days of thy presence and thy meeting, and the love which took from thy grasp the reins of patience and forbearance, and brought thee time and again to this place wherein the Call hath been raised morning and evening.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling ‘Alí that the Wronged One remembers in the prison of ‘Akká the days of his presence and the love that drew him there again and again; remembered visits from the side of the Remembered.

selected.text: The family of His Holiness Nabil is associated with His Holiness the Glorious One, for in truth for sixty years that family has been serving the Threshold with the utmost faith and certitude. In every instance they were firm and in every station they were steadfast. This family, nay this lineage, possess eternal glory and heavenly bounty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on the family of Nabíl, which for sixty years served the Threshold with firmness in every instance; a family’s sustained service.

selected.text: Reflect upon the crimson leaf, upon whom be all the most glorious Glory of God. In view of the love and enkindlement and yearning and attraction that was in her, God, exalted and mighty be He, made her the object of mentions, for there was revealed in her honor that which shall endure as long as the kingdom of earth and heaven shall last.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on the crimson leaf, for whose love and yearning there was revealed what shall endure as long as earth and heaven last; a woman’s enduring revealed memorial.

selected.text: Real feasts were held during the days of the Blessed Perfection; for then we used to get up early morning with the utmost joy, exhilaration and happiness, addressing ourselves with transport:- 'This is the day of the Feast. Soon shall we stand before His Holiness Baha'u'llah, receive a new Grace and witness a new Confirmation and Bounty.'
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalling the real feasts in the days of Bahá’u’lláh, when they rose early with joy to stand before Him; a joyful shared memory.

selected.text: The honored Nightingale of the garden of meanings, the trusted messenger of the All-Merciful, His Holiness Shaykh Salman, upon him be the fragrances of his Lord, the Bestower, rendered outstanding services to the Cause of God. His mention should always remain in spiritual gatherings, for in the Abha Kingdom he shines like a brilliant lamp.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on Shaykh Salmán, the trusted messenger, whose mention should always remain in spiritual gatherings; asks for ongoing remembrance.

selected.text: We desired to make mention of one of My maidservants who turned toward My horizon and hastened to the Dawning-Place of the light of My countenance until she entered My abode and stood before the throne of My grandeur, and her eyes were solaced by My beauty, and she drank the choice wine of reunion in her final days from the cup of My bounty.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh on a maidservant who entered His abode and drank the wine of reunion in her final days; a woman’s journey ending in presence.

selected.text: We make mention in this place of thy father who was adorned with the ornament of the loving-kindness of his Lord, the All-Merciful. He hath ascended unto God and the Concourse on High found from him the fragrance of My love, the Mighty, the Inaccessible. Blessed is he and blessed is he who remembereth him, and woe unto every heedless doubter.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that a father’s ascension carried the fragrance of His love and that blessed is he who remembers him; revealed warrant for remembrance.

selected.text: Thy distinguished grandfather, Mirza Jalal, was illumined by the lights of the Beauty of God. Praise be to God that until his last breath he was intimate with the mention of the Beloved of the horizons and was firm and steadfast in the Cause. In truth, he was the brilliant lamp of that family and now shineth in the niche of the supreme realm.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá on a grandfather, Mírzá Jalál, firm until his last breath and the brilliant lamp of his family; ancestry and steadfastness.

selected.text: Thy respected wife, Mrs. Maxwell, is indeed a lighted candle. Know thou her worth. That maidservant of God shall shine forth in the spiritual gatherings in such wise as to surpass the fame of Mary Magdalene and St. Barbara. That lamp of the love of God is in truth aglow and will be the cause of thy glory in this world and in the Kingdom above
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praising the living Mrs. Maxwell to her husband as a lighted candle whose worth he should know; an example of praise for a living friend.

selected.text: O ye two remnants of the two noble souls, `Abdu'l-Majid and Siyyid Muhsin. The truth is that I find myself incapable of befittingly extolling those two blessed souls. Both were taught by the Blessed Beauty, were revived by the Fragrances of the Holy Spirit, and they both, like unto immovable mountains remained firm, steadfast and strong in Iraq
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to the survivors of ‘Abdu’l-Majíd and Siyyid Muḥsin, both taught by the Blessed Beauty and firm as immovable mountains in Iraq; a family letter naming its subjects.

selected.text: She never wavered in serving Thy loved ones and comforting Thy servants. She spent her wealth upon the weak and the poor, seeking Thy good pleasure … She was a treasure to every poor one, a shelter to every captive, a refuge to every stranger. Her generosity was as a flowing spring to every thirsty soul, and a comfort to every wanderer and wayfarer
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for a woman who spent her wealth on the weak and was a shelter to every captive and stranger; shows generosity as the substance of praise.

selected.text: We were with him at the time of his ascension and made mention of him in such wise as caused the ocean of forgiveness to surge and the fragrances of God's tender mercy, the Forgiving, the Merciful, to waft. Blessed is he and blessed is he who maketh mention of him after his ascension through that which hath been sent down from One ancient in descent.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh that He was with a believer at his ascension and that blessed is he who mentions him after it with the revealed words; revealed warrant for remembrance.

selected.text: How fair art thou in my sight! Will I ever see thee again with my physical eyes? Will I ever walk through thy narrow streets? Art thou not the city wherein Baha'u'llah spent His earthly life and then ascended to the supreme Concourse?
